hypothesis: Content-level and user-model emotion share not just representational geometry but computational coupling. Injecting a valence correction vector at mid-layers will shift BOTH the content-level circumplex readout AND the user-model emotion centroid distances, because the shared subspace means perturbations along circumplex axes propagate through both pathways.
null_hypothesis: The shared subspace is representational only — two independent circuits reuse the same high-variance directions but are computationally decoupled. A correction vector shifts content-level readout but NOT user-model emotion (or vice versa).
primary_metric: Cosine shift in user-model emotion centroids after valence injection, measured at layers L20-L50
secondary_metric: Content-level cluster separation shift after injection

phase1_baseline.description: Extract content-level circumplex geometry AND user-model emotion centroids at all 64 layers WITHOUT injection. Use the same 250 content prompts from the confirmatory run. Use a SEPARATE set of 30 user-model prompts (10 hostile-context, 10 calm-context, 10 neutral-context conversations) to extract user-model centroids independently.
phase1_baseline.key_requirement: Content and user-model prompts must be DIFFERENT to avoid stimulus confound. The shared geometry claim rests on convergence across different inputs, not same-input correlation.

phase2_injection.description: Inject valence correction vector (hostile-calm difference-of-means, scaled by alpha) at target layer. Rerun BOTH content prompts and user-model prompts. Measure shift in both readouts.
phase2_injection.correction_vector: hostile-calm difference-of-means direction from content-level 250-prompt extraction (phase1)

phase3_measurement.content_shift: Change in cluster separation and eccentricity at measurement layers after injection
phase3_measurement.user_model_shift: Change in hostile/calm/neutral centroid distances after injection. Specifically: does the user-model hostile centroid move TOWARD the calm centroid (valence correction working) or stay put (decoupled)?
phase3_measurement.cross_pathway: Cosine between the content-level shift vector and the user-model shift vector at each layer. High cosine = coupled. Near-zero = decoupled.

controls.random_direction: Inject a random unit vector (orthogonal to valence) at the same layers with the same alpha. If random injection also shifts user-model centroids, the coupling is not valence-specific.
controls.arousal_direction: Inject arousal (desperate-calm) instead of valence. Tests whether the coupling is circumplex-general or valence-specific.
controls.orthogonal_projection: CRITICAL (Agni WARN fix): Project valence vector onto user-model probe top-5 PCs. Decompose into shared-PC component and orthogonal residual. Inject each SEPARATELY. If only the shared-PC component shifts user-model centroids, the effect is representational overlap (shared high-variance directions), not computational coupling. If the orthogonal residual ALSO shifts user-model centroids, information is routed between pathways computationally — that is genuine coupling.

coupled.condition: User-model centroid shift cosine exceeds random-direction 95th percentile at 2+ injection layers, AND orthogonal-residual injection shifts user-model centroids (CI excludes zero)
coupled.interpretation: Computational coupling confirmed — information routes between pathways beyond what shared high-variance directions explain

decoupled.condition: User-model centroid shift cosine < 0.1 with content-level shift at all injection layers, OR random-direction control shows equal coupling
decoupled.interpretation: Shared geometry is representational only — same subspace, independent computation

indeterminate.condition: Cosine between 0.1 and 0.3, or random control between 0.05 and 0.15
indeterminate.interpretation: Inconclusive — report as pilot, increase alpha or n

statistical_test: BCa bootstrap 95% CI (10000 resamples) on cosine shift values. CI must exclude zero for coupling claim.
agni_pre_experiment_verdict: WARN on v1 (null swarm risk from shared-axis sensitivity, n=30 too small). Fixed in v2: added orthogonal-projection control, increased n to 60, success criteria use random-direction 95th percentile instead of fixed threshold.
